query: How does resolution time vary by agent and issue type?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is simply the focus variable itself (resolution_time expressed in hours). It restates the focus and offers no external variable to segment or compare against. Its continuous, highly fine-grained values cannot serve as a grouping dimension.

per_column.name: agent_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This is a per-agent aggregate of the focus variable, not an external associational variable. It is derived directly from resolution_time and effectively pre-computes the answer the query seeks rather than opening an independent relationship. The agent identity itself already exists in the table (assigned_to); this column just leaks the target mean, which is circular for EDA.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Same issue: a per-category mean of the focus variable. Category already exists as a genuine segmentation dimension; this column merely encodes the focus aggregated by it, which is target restatement rather than an external explanatory variable.

per_column.name: agent_category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: A two-way aggregate of the focus variable itself. It is an opaque continuous score derived from resolution_time, not an interpretable, well-separated category to group on. It restates the answer to the query rather than enabling independent exploration.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns introduce an external, associational variable. The first is the focus itself; the remaining three are group-wise averages of the focus (by agent, by category, by agent-and-category). These are direct aggregations/leakage of resolution_time and simply pre-bake the very comparison the query asks for, rather than providing new interpretable dimensions to segment on. Genuine segmentation variables (agent, category, priority) already exist in the original table; the augmentation added nothing external. All values are fine-grained continuous means with no well-separated categories, failing the interpretability requirement. This set does not realise the exploratory-analysis claim.
